newsitem.title: USA: Ill. lawmakers give agency expanded bond authority.
newsitem.headline: Ill. lawmakers give agency expanded bond authority.

text.p: Illinois Development Finance Authority Director Bobby Wilkerson has said state lawmakers approved legislation expanding its bond authorization by $2.9 billion during their recent session.
The measure approved by lawmakers on June 1 in the closing minutes of the session has not yet reached Gov. Jim Edgar's desk, a legislative research aide said Monday.

The bill gives the authority permission to issue another $1.5 billion of general debt, $900 million of environmental bonds and $500 million of local government debt, Wilkerson said in an interview late Friday.
Bonds issued by the authority are neither legal nor moral obligations of state, and the borrower is responsible for payment of the debt, Wilkerson noted.
The authority receives no state funding and operates as the equivalent of a private business, Wilkerson said.
The authority has approximately $5 billion of outstanding debt, Wilkerson said. It had a very successful month in May and expects to close fiscal 1997 with a good month as well, he added.
The authorization would have immediate effect upon the governor's signature.
